craft_notes: Sthāyin: wonder edged with dread (the body answers). Sanskrit first: two tremors (heart, palate-gate), one whirl (head), the naming (sight-transmission sign) → L4 sets tremors line 1, whirl+naming line 2. Rows: row 1 (sign-last — lakṣaṇam closes as 'crossing-state' closes). Rupture: dash after 'gate' — trembling held, whirling released. Close: end-weight on the technical term (kept compound-literal, un-smoothed). Minimal pass: 'crossing-state' for saṃkrānti-lakṣaṇa (crossing singable, transmission in cite). Read aloud: line 1 shakes (tremble/gate short), dash, line 2 spins then names (spins/crossing-state). Rejected: 'dizzy' for bhramate — killed: whirl is cosmic motion, dizzy is ailment; softening the dread — killed: bhaya is IN the body here, song must carry it.

lines: First the heart will tremble, then the palate-gate —
the head spins: this is the sight's crossing-state.
l4.sanskrit_cite: hṛdayaṃ kampate pūrvaṃ tālukadvārameva ca / śiraśca bhramate tasya dṛṣṭisaṃkrāntilakṣaṇam

reads_against.argmap: The stage-signs begin in the body: trembling heart, palate gate, whirling head — the mark of sight-transmission.
c1_essence: Heart trembles first, palate gate, head whirls — sight-transmission's sign.
reads_against.c1_rasa: adbhuta strained toward bhayānaka (wonder edged with fear)
